candidates.reason: Best of the three: the LUST/FOR/WIN lockup is scaled to the full 160 px width, so it stays readable and is clearly the focal point. But LUST and WIN run almost to the side edges with about 10 px of margin. The four corner x-marks float at roughly y=85 and y=512 instead of framing the canvas corners. The photo crop is mostly black hand wrap, and the boxer's torso, which gave the original its impact, is lost.

The lockup is shrunk to about 60% of the width, and the small x-row and the FOR box are near illegible at this size. The corner x-marks sit at arbitrary mid-canvas heights (about y=140 and y=455), so they read as stray specks rather than a frame. Large dark areas above and below the small lockup leave the poster without a strong focal point.

The weakest: the lockup is the smallest of the three (about 45% of the width), so the FOR box text and the row of x-marks are tiny and weak against the busy dark photo. The corner marks are clustered close above and below the lockup (about y=225 and y=370), so they read as clutter, not a frame. The rest of the tall canvas is dead image, and the brand mark is trivialised.
